runs.text: The document reports no dissolution of PVDF binder by ethylene glycol. It states that the PVDF binder was

runs.quote: not removed or dissolved during the EG-based separation

runs.text: process, and FTIR and EDX spectra were used to confirm this. The authors also state that the separation

runs.quote: does not remove PVDF binder from the cathode

runs.text: particles. They explain this with Hansen solubility parameters: EG has a high HSP distance (Ra) to PVDF, which indicates low ability to dissolve it. The document therefore gives no quantity for any dissolved PVDF fraction; by the authors' account none was dissolved. Delamination instead works by competitive inhibition of the PVDF hydrogen bonding, not by dissolving the binder.

The authors also state that the separation does not remove PVDF binder from the cathode[2] particles. They explain this with Hansen solubility parameters: EG has a high HSP distance (Ra) to PVDF, which indicates low ability to dissolve it. The document therefore gives no quantity for any dissolved PVDF fraction; by the authors' account none was dissolved. Delamination instead works by competitive inhibition of the PVDF hydrogen bonding, not by dissolving the binder.
